title: When did the Cold War actually end ?
fullText: The end of the Cold War conjures up images of jubilant crowds atop the Berlin Wall  hammers chipping away at concrete and the red flag being lowered from the Kremlin on Christmas Day  it was the moment communism lost capitalism won and the world sorted itself out  into one block instead of two  and whilst most people would tell you this happened in 1989 or maybe 1991 when you actually ask a historian the answer is much more nebulous with some of the participants themselves disagreeing about whether it's over yet now, obviously given that the Cold War wasn't actually a war choosing a definitive ending day is going to be difficult it's not like there was ever a formal ceasefire between two sides  who spent the whole time insisting they weren't fighting so  when is the earliest you could say this ends well depending on whose perspective you're looking through it was pretty early as early as 1985 when Mikhail Gorbachev took over in Moscow he made it clear that the Soviet Union was done treating the Cold War as an eternal contest he signed nuclear reduction treaties with Reagan pulled Soviet troops out of Afghanistan and in 1988  a Soviet advisor named Georgi Arbatov told an American reporter that Moscow had a secret weapon it was about to unleash  his words we're going to do a terrible thing to you we are going to deprive you of an enemy whether the Americans took him seriously is unclear at least one of them was ahead of schedule A US State Department official named Francis Fukuyama had already declared the end of history in the summer of 1989 months before the Berlin Wall came down history as it would turn out had not been consulted because the moment most people point to is the actual end of the Cold War was still a few weeks away and when it came  it came by accident on the evening of November 9th, 1989 an East German official named Gunther Schabowski held a live broadcast press conference to announce new travel rules for East Berliners he had been handed the memo minutes before hadn't actually read it and when a reporter asked  when the rules took effect he flipped through his papers  and said  essentially immediately  I think  the memo actually said the next day within hours tens of thousands of East Berliners were climbing the wall while confused border guards decided not to shoot them the event that supposedly ended the Cold War was in the strictest technical sense an administrative typo three weeks later George H. W. Bush and Gorbachev met on a pair of ships off the coast of Malta and declared that the world was leaving the epoch of Cold War  and entering a new one no treaty was signed no document was drafted they just  sort of, said it out loud and most historians will happily tell you Malta is where the Cold War ended uh which would be more convincing if the Warsaw Pact hadn't gone on existing for another 19 months which is quite a long time for an alliance to outlive its own war or if the country supposedly ending the war on equal terms hadn't been in the middle of losing it now if what you want is an actual document there is one in November 1990 34 nations gathered in Paris and signed the charter for a new Europe formally declaring that the era of confrontation and division in Europe had ended it's the closest thing to an official ending the Cold War ever got signed dated and witnessed which would make it the obvious answer if anyone outside of diplomatic circles had ever heard of it nowhere is the confusion about whether the war was over clearer than in a speech George H. W. Bush gave in Kiev on August 1st, 1991 speaking to the Ukrainian parliament he warned them not to declare independence describing local nationalism as suicidal the speech would come to be nicknamed the 'Chicken Kiev speech' less than three weeks later Soviet hardliners tried to overthrow Gorbachev in a coup they failed within 72 hours and Ukraine declared independence two days after that by Christmas the country Bush had warned them not to leave no longer existed which brings us to the actual end of the Soviet Union which happened not in a treaty room not at a summit but at a hunting lodge in a Belarusian forest on December 8th, 1991 three men Boris Yeltsin of Russia  Leonid Kravchuk of Ukraine and a Belarusian physicist named Stanislav Shushkevich held a secret meeting at a place called Viskuli Shushkevich had actually invited Yeltsin over to negotiate oil and gas supplies because Belarus was heading into winter without contracts somewhere between drinks Yeltsin's deputy Gennady Burbulis suggested they might as well sign a single sentence declaring that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist their legal justification was that Russia Ukraine and Belarus had been founding signatories of the 1922 treaty that created the USSR so the logic went they were perfectly entitled to uncreate it Gorbachev was not invited neither was Nursultan Nazarbayev of Kazakhstan the man Gorbachev was counting on to hold the union together which probably had something to do with him not being Slavic four days later the Russian parliament ratified the dissolution of its own country with only a handful of deputies voting against on Christmas Day Gorbachev went on television and resigned that evening the red flag with the hammer and sickle came down from the Kremlin it's genuinely hard to think of another superpower in history that ended its own existence this administratively and that would be a satisfying place to end the story if the Cold War had only ever existed in Europe but it hadn't Roughly 8,000 miles from Berlin in Havana nobody was celebrating Cuba had been receiving Soviet subsidies that made up something like a third of its entire economy in three years from 1990 to 1993 its GDP fell by around 35% food and fuel imports collapsed and the average Cuban lost around 10 pounds of body weight Havana buses stopped running because there was no fuel the state produced 1 million Chinese made bicycles to replace them people kept chickens on their balconies the government officially called it the Special Period in time of peace which is a pretty polite way to describe three years of rationing blackouts and severe hunger Cubans still call it that today North Korea took a bit longer to feel it when it did it was worse Soviet fuel had been running the tractors Soviet fertilizer had been feeding the soil when both stopped arriving agriculture collapsed within a single growing season Between 1994 and 1998 in an episode Pyongyang officially named the Arduous March  somewhere between 600,000 and 1 million North Koreans died of starvation depending on which estimate you believe in Berlin they were dancing on the wall in Havana and Pyongyang the end of the Cold War arrived as the collapse of the calorie supply which is why the question when did the Cold War actually end is really a different question in disguise it's a question about what the Cold War was to begin with if you define it as an ideological contest between a communist east and a capitalist west then yes it ended around 1989 when East Germans stopped believing the state and started believing television but if you define it as a great power competition between Moscow and Washington over who gets to draw the map then it's much harder to argue it ever ended at all also a growing number of historians would tell you it just went on holiday for about a decade before quietly resuming these two definitions used to be the same thing that was the whole point of the Cold War they came apart the moment Moscow stopped exporting an ideology and started just being a country again for much of the world the question is even simpler in Beijing the ruling party looked at what happened to the Soviet Union and drew the exact opposite lesson from the one western analysts expected that reform kills communism and therefore reform must be prevented at all costs in Pyongyang  Havana  and Hanoi one party states that outlasted their patron are still in power today the Cold War in other words didn't end it ended in Europe in much of Asia and the Caribbean nobody sent an invitation and so whilst 1989 is not exactly a perfect ending date for something as nebulous as the Cold War it's probably one of the better ones for the people who won it because let's be reasonable we're almost certainly never going to get an agreed upon end I hope you enjoyed this episode
